providers.reason: The stock has significant near-term catalysts following shareholder approval for the spinoff of its large materials trading unit (tk accelis), expected by October. Recent narrowing of its 2026 profit outlook to the higher end and a restructuring agreement with the IG Metall union signal improving operational control and structural simplification.
providers.risk: Deep projected net losses for 2026 due to heavy restructuring provisions and volatile global steel demand.

providers.reason: Steel guidance was raised, Deutsche Bank lifted its target to €18 with a Buy rating, and the stock gained roughly 6% Friday and another ~3% Monday. A capital markets day at end-September offers a further catalyst, giving thyssenkrupp the strongest stock-specific momentum on the list.
providers.risk: After a ~21% gain in 30 days the share is extended; profit-taking or any disappointment heading into the late-September capital markets day could trigger a sharp pullback.

providers.reason: TKMS spin trading planned Oct 20 with thyssenkrupp retaining 51% and EUR18.6bn backlog booked to 2040s plus F127 option. DZ Bank upgraded to Buy Aug 21, lifting fair value EUR11 to EUR16 on TKMS sum-of-parts.
providers.risk: Steel restructuring, ~EUR10bn TKMS guarantee renegotiation and distant Oct 20 listing leave execution and funding risk if tape stays weak.

providers.reason: 63% YTD gain; Q3 revenue +8% to €8.8bn, TK Accelis 49% spin-off on track for Oct listing. Deutsche Bank raised PT to €18 (Buy).
providers.risk: Steel sector cyclical weakness or delayed spin-off execution.

providers.reason: The stock has shown significant momentum with a 12% rise over the last month, supported by strategic restructuring including the tk accelis spin-off. Technical indicators like the 3-month MACD and short-term moving averages remain positive, and analysts have recently revised fair value estimates upward to €22.00.
providers.risk: Cyclical downturn in European steel demand and execution risks surrounding the complex separation of its materials and steel units.

providers.reason: Thyssenkrupp trades near its 52-week high after a 24% 30-day run, supported by Deutsche Bank's Buy rating and €18 target, up from €16. Restructuring momentum remains the dominant driver, and the current risk-on tape favors continuation of the technical trend.
providers.risk: The stock is extended with roughly 49% realized volatility; fading restructuring or anchor-investor speculation could trigger sharp profit-taking.
